items.title: 4.7.1 Strategy for the identification of limiting reactant (limiting reactant pehchanne ka tareeqa) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 4.7.1, printed pages 86-87, with Sample Problems 4.17 and 4.18 worked.

blocks.text: Limiting reactant pehchanne ke liye yeh teen steps (qadam) kiye jate hain:

items: Reactants ki di hui amounts se un ke moles nikalein.
Balanced chemical equation ki madad se dekhein ke har reactant se product ke kitne moles banenge.
Jo reactant sab se kam product de, woh limiting reactant hai; doosra excess reactant hai.

blocks.title: Did You Know? (kya aap jante hain?)
blocks.text: Aag ek combustion reaction hai jis mein fuel aur oxygen, O₂, aam taur par zyada temperature par mil kar pani aur carbon dioxide banate hain. Aag ek dafa lag jaye to khud chalti rehti hai. Aag bujhane ka acha tareeqa smothering (dhaanp dena) hai, jo oxygen ko us had se kam kar deta hai jo jalne ke liye zaroori hai. Yani smothering excess reactant (oxygen) ko kam karti hai. Foam, inert gas aur CO₂ is kaam ke liye achhe hain.
Neeche diya gaya sawal is baat ko saaf karega.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.17 (Limiting reactant)
blocks.problem: 18.1 g NH₃ (molar mass 17.0 g mol⁻¹) aur 90.4 g CuO (molar mass 79.5 g mol⁻¹) se kitna N₂ banega? 2NH₃(g) + 3CuO(s) → N₂(g) + 3Cu(s) + 3H₂O(g)
steps: CuO : N₂ = 3 : 1, to CuO se N₂ = 1/3 × 1.14 = 0.38 mol
NH₃ : N₂ = 2 : 1, to NH₃ se N₂ = 1/2 × 1.06 = 0.53 mol
CuO kam N₂ deta hai, is liye CuO limiting reactant hai; N₂ = 0.38 mol
N₂ ka mass = n x M = 0.38 mol x 28.0 g mol⁻¹

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne N₂ ka mass 0.38 mol x 17.0 g mol⁻¹ = 9.0 g nikala hai. 17.0 ammonia (NH₃) ka molar mass hai; N₂ ka molar mass 28.0 g mol⁻¹ hai, is liye sahi mass 0.38 x 28.0 = 10.6 g hai. Sawal mein NH₃ ka mass 1.81 g chhapa hai magar solution (hal) 18.1 g istemal karta hai (18.1 ÷ 17.0 = 1.06 mol); yahan solution ke mutabiq 18.1 g liya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 4.18 (Limiting reactant)
blocks.problem: Na₂SO₄ aur Pb(NO₃)₂ ke solutions milane se PbSO₄ ka precipitate (neeche baithne wala solid) banta hai. 1.25 dm³ 0.05 mol dm⁻³ Pb(NO₃)₂ aur 2.00 dm³ 0.025 mol dm⁻³ Na₂SO₄ milane se kitna PbSO₄ banega? Na₂SO₄(aq) + Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2NaNO₃(aq)
steps: Net ionic equation: Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s)
Formula: moles = concentration x volume (n = CV)
Pb²⁺ ke moles = 0.05 mol dm⁻³ × 1.25 dm³ = 0.0625 mol
SO₄²⁻ ke moles = 0.025 mol dm⁻³ × 2.00 dm³ = 0.05 mol
Ratio 1 : 1 hai; SO₄²⁻ (0.05 mol) Pb²⁺ (0.0625 mol) se kam hai, is liye SO₄²⁻ limiting hai aur sirf 0.05 mol PbSO₄ banega
PbSO₄ ka molar mass = 303.3 g mol⁻¹
blocks.answer: Mass = 0.05 mol × 303.3 g mol⁻¹ = 15.2 g PbSO₄

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki equation balanced nahi: baen taraf 2 Na hain aur daen taraf 1. Sahi: Na₂SO₄(aq) + Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2NaNO₃(aq). Pb²⁺ aur SO₄²⁻ ka 1 : 1 ratio aur jawab is se nahi badalte.

items: Teen steps: har reactant ke moles; equation se har ek ka product; sab se kam product dene wala limiting.
Sample 4.17 mein CuO limiting (0.38 mol N₂ = 10.6 g); Sample 4.18 mein SO₄²⁻ limiting (0.05 mol, 15.2 g PbSO₄).
